primary_diagnosis_treated: Uncontrolled essential hypertension associated with metabolic syndrome
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG136 (Hypertension) and NICE CG181/PH46 (Metabolic syndrome components)

medications.duration: Ongoing – review BP and metabolic profile annually
medications.nice_justification: Thiazide diuretic is an acceptable second‑line antihypertensive per NG136; retained pending ACE‑I optimisation
Management of B12‑deficiency anaemia per standard practice; no conflict with NICE hypertension or metabolic‑syndrome guidance

medications.duration: Lifelong — review BP, renal function and potassium at 2 weeks, then annually
medications.purpose: First‑line treatment of essential hypertension; renal‑protective in metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line for non‑Afro‑Caribbean adults <55 y with hypertension

medications.duration: Lifelong — review BP after 4–6 weeks; titrate to 10 mg if needed; then annual review
medications.purpose: Add‑on antihypertensive if target <140/90 mmHg not achieved with ACE‑I alone
medications.nice_justification: NG136 recommends a CCB as preferred second‑line agent or part of combination therapy when BP remains uncontrolled

medications.duration: Lifelong — lipid profile at 12 weeks, then annually
medications.purpose: Reduce cardiovascular risk associated with metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: CG181/NG136 advise statin therapy for patients with QRISK ≥10 % or ≥2 metabolic‑syndrome components

medications.dose: 200 mg oral tablet once daily with food
medications.duration: Continue 3 months after ferritin normalisation; re‑check Hb & ferritin at 8 weeks
medications.purpose: Treat iron‑deficiency anaemia (if iron studies confirm deficiency)
medications.nice_justification: CG181 recommends oral iron as first‑line for confirmed iron‑deficiency anaemia

medications.dose: 500 mg oral tablet once daily with evening meal (titrate by 500 mg weekly to 1 g BID as tolerated)
medications.duration: Lifelong — HbA1c review every 3 months; renal function review at 3 months and annually
medications.purpose: Improve glycaemic control in pre‑diabetes with high cardiovascular risk
medications.nice_justification: NICE PH38/NG28 recommend metformin for high‑risk pre‑diabetes when BMI ≥30 kg/m² and no renal contraindication

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive antihypertensive effect may cause symptomatic hypotension, especially after first ACE‑I dose
interactions_checked.action: Start ramipril at low dose, monitor BP and symptoms; consider reducing or stopping hydrochlorothiazide once target BP achieved

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive BP‑lowering effect; no pharmacokinetic interaction
interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP after adding amlodipine; adjust hydrochlorothiazide dose if needed

interactions_checked.interaction: Thiazide may increase glucose, potentially counteracting metformin
interactions_checked.action: Emphasise lifestyle measures; monitor fasting glucose/HbA1c

contraindications.reason: Renal function (eGFR) not yet known; metformin contraindicated if eGFR <30 ml/min/1.73 m² and dose‑adjusted if 30‑45
contraindications.alternative: Obtain eGFR; if eGFR ≥45 start low‑dose metformin, otherwise hold

assumptions_warnings: eGFR, serum potassium and liver function tests are not available – assumed normal for initial ACE‑I dosing; will be measured before titration.
QRISK score not calculated – assumed ≥10 % based on hypertension, obesity, pre‑diabetes.
Lipid profile missing – will be obtained to confirm dyslipidaemia before statin initiation.
Iron studies (ferritin, TSAT) not performed – ferrous sulphate pending confirmation of iron deficiency.
Allergy status unknown – will verify no ACE‑I or statin hypersensitivity.
Pregnancy status not documented – will confirm patient is not pregnant before starting ACE‑I.
treatment_summary: Start low‑dose ramipril and replace or taper hydrochlorothiazide as BP improves; add amlodipine if target <140/90 mmHg not reached after 4–6 weeks. Initiate atorvastatin 20 mg nightly for cardiovascular risk reduction. Arrange baseline labs (eGFR, electrolytes, LFTs, fasting lipids, iron studies) and calculate QRISK. Pending normal eGFR, consider metformin for pre‑diabetes and ferrous sulphate if iron deficiency is confirmed. Continue existing vitamin B12 therapy. Monitor BP, renal function, potassium, lipid profile and HbA1c according to NICE NG136 and CG181 recommendations.
